transcript.en: Adam: So, Michelle, shall we make a start on our presentation? We haven't got that much time left.
transcript.zh: 那么，米歇尔，我们开始做演示吧？我们剩下的时间不多了。

transcript.en: Michelle: No, Adam. But at least we've done all the background reading. I found it really interesting – I'd never even heard of the Laki eruption before this.
transcript.zh: 不，亚当。但至少我们已经做了所有的背景阅读。我觉得真的很有趣——在这之前我甚至从未听说过Laki火山爆发。

transcript.en: Adam: Me neither. I suppose 1783 is a long time ago.
transcript.zh: 我也是。我想1783年确实是很久以前了。

transcript.en: Michelle: But it was a huge eruption and it had such devastating consequences.
transcript.zh: 但那次是一次巨大的火山爆发，造成了灾难性的后果。

transcript.en: Adam: I know. It was great there were so many primary sources to look at. It really gives you a sense of how catastrophic the volcano was.
transcript.zh: 我知道。很幸运有这么多一手资料供我们查阅。它真正让你感受到这座火山有多么灾难性。

transcript.en: People were really trying to make sense of the science for the first time.
transcript.zh: 人们当时真的在努力首次理解这个科学现象。

transcript.en: Michelle: That's right. But what I found more significant was how it impacted directly and indirectly on political events, as well as having massive social and economic consequences.
transcript.zh: 没错。但我认为更重要的是它如何直接和间接地影响了政治事件，以及产生了巨大的社会和经济后果。

transcript.en: Adam: I know. That should be the main focus of our presentation.
transcript.zh: 我知道。这应该是我们演示的主要焦点。

transcript.en: Michelle: The observations made by people at the time were interesting, weren't they?
transcript.zh: 当时人们的观察很有意思，不是吗？

transcript.en: I mean, they all gave a pretty consistent account of what happened, even if they didn't always use the same terminology.
transcript.zh: 我的意思是，他们都对所发生的事情给出了相当一致的描述，即使他们并不总是使用相同的术语。

transcript.en: Adam: Yeah. I was surprised there were so many weather stations established by that time – so, you know, you can see how the weather changed, often by the hour.
transcript.zh: 是的。我对当时已经建立了这么多气象站感到惊讶——你知道，你可以看到天气是如何变化的，通常每小时一变。

transcript.en: Michelle: Right. Writers at the time talked about the Laki haze to describe the volcanic fog that spread across Europe.
transcript.zh: 对。当时的作家们谈论到"Laki haze"，用来描述蔓延到欧洲的火山雾。

transcript.en: They all realised that this wasn't the sort of fog they were used to – and of course this was in pre-industrial times – so they hadn't experienced sulphur-smelling fog before.
transcript.zh: 他们都意识到这不是他们所熟悉的那种雾气——当然那是在工业前时代——所以他们以前没有经历过有硫磺气味的雾气。

transcript.en: Adam: No, that's true.
transcript.zh: 是的，没错。

transcript.en: Michelle: Reports from the period blamed the haze for an increase in headaches, respiratory issues and asthma attacks. And they all describe how it covered the sun and made it look a strange red colour.
transcript.zh: 当时的报告将这种雾气归咎于引发头痛、呼吸问题和哮喘发作的增加。他们还都描述了如何遮蔽了阳光并使其呈现奇怪的红色。

transcript.en: Adam: Must have been very weird.
transcript.zh: 一定很奇怪。

transcript.en: Michelle: It's interesting that Benjamin Franklin wrote about the haze. Did you read that? He was the American ambassador in Paris at the time.
transcript.zh: 有趣的是本杰明·富兰克林也写了关于这种雾气的文章。你读过吗？他当时是驻巴黎的美国大使。

transcript.en: Adam: Yeah. At first no one realised that the haze was caused by the volcanic eruption in Iceland.
transcript.zh: 是的。起初没有人意识到这种雾气是由冰岛的火山爆发引起的。

transcript.en: Michelle: It was Benjamin Franklin who realised that before anyone else.
transcript.zh: 是本杰明·富兰克林比其他人先意识到这一点。

transcript.en: Adam: He's often credited with that, apparently. But a French naturalist beat him to it – I can't remember his name. I'd have to look it up.
transcript.zh: 他通常被认为是第一个意识到的人，显然。但有一位法国博物学家比他更早，我记不得他的名字了。我得查一下。

transcript.en: Then other naturalists had the same idea – all independently of each other.
transcript.zh: 然后其他博物学家也有了同样的想法——都是独立思考的。

transcript.en: Michelle: Oh right. We should talk about the immediate impact of the eruption, which was obviously enormous – especially in Iceland, where so many people died.
transcript.zh: 哦，对。我们应该谈谈火山爆发的直接影响，显然是巨大的——尤其是在冰岛，那里有这么多人死亡。

transcript.en: Adam: Mmm. You'd expect that – and the fact that the volcanic ash drifted so swiftly – but not that the effects would go on for so long.
transcript.zh: 嗯。这是可以预料的——以及火山灰的迅速飘散——但不会预料到影响会持续这么久。

transcript.en: Or that two years after the eruption, strange weather events were being reported as far away as North America and North Africa.
transcript.zh: 火山爆发两年后，甚至在北美和北非都出现了奇怪的天气事件。

transcript.en: Michelle: No. I found all that hard to believe too. It must have been terrible – and there was nothing anyone could do about it, even if they knew the ash cloud was coming in their direction.
transcript.zh: 是的。我也觉得这一切很难以置信。一定很可怕——而且无论他们知道灰云朝他们方向飘来，也无法做任何事情。

transcript.en: Michelle: We should run through some of the terrible consequences of the eruption experienced in different countries. There's quite a varied range.
transcript.zh: 我们应该简要介绍一下不同国家在火山爆发中经历的可怕后果。范围相当广泛。

transcript.en: Adam: Starting with Iceland, where the impact on farming was devastating.
transcript.zh: 首先是冰岛，在那里农业受到了毁灭性的影响。

transcript.en: Michelle: Mmm. One of the most dramatic things there was the effect on livestock as they grazed in the fields.
transcript.zh: 嗯。那里最令人震惊的事情之一是牲畜在田野中吃草时受到的影响。

transcript.en: They were poisoned because they ate vegetation that had been contaminated with fluorine as a result of the volcanic fallout.
transcript.zh: 它们中毒了，因为它们吃了因火山落尘而被氟污染的植被。

transcript.en: Adam: That was horrible. In Egypt, the bizarre weather patterns led to a severe drought and as a result the Nile didn't flood, which meant the crops all failed.
transcript.zh: 那真是可怕。在埃及，奇特的气候模式导致了严重的干旱，结果尼罗河没有泛滥，作物全都失败了。

transcript.en: Michelle: It's so far from where the eruption happened and yet the famine there led to more people dying than any other country. It was worse than the plague.
transcript.zh: 这离火山爆发发生的地方很远，但饥荒导致的死亡人数比其他任何国家都多。比瘟疫还严重。

transcript.en: Adam: OK. Then in the UK the mortality rate went up a lot – presumably from respiratory illnesses.
transcript.zh: 好。然后在英国，死亡率大大增加——可能是因为呼吸系统疾病。

transcript.en: According to one report it was about double the usual number and included an unusually high percentage of people under the age of 25.
transcript.zh: 根据一份报告，死亡人数是平时的两倍，其中年龄不到25岁的人比例异常高。

transcript.en: Michelle: Mmm. I think people will be surprised to hear that the weather in the USA was badly affected too..
transcript.zh: 嗯。我觉得人们听到美国的天气也受到了严重影响会感到惊讶。

transcript.en: George Washington even makes a note in his diary that they were snowbound until March in Virginia. That was before he became president.
transcript.zh: 乔治·华盛顿甚至在他的日记中记录了，弗吉尼亚州直到三月都被大雪困住。那是他成为总统之前的事情。

transcript.en: Adam: Yes, and there was ice floating down the Mississippi, which was unprecedented.
transcript.zh: 是的，还有密西西比河上漂浮的冰，这是前所未有的。

transcript.en: Michelle: Astonishing, really. Anyway, what do you think …
transcript.zh: 真是令人惊讶。总之，你觉得...
